# CloudBitmaps

> Distributed, cloud-native Roaring Bitmaps. Query and intersect billion-scale integer sets over tiered
> cloud storage (RAM → warm NoSQL/SQL → cold immutable objects) at a fraction of an always-on cache, with
> the familiar in-memory API: `add`, `has`, `remove`, `count`, `intersect`.

CloudBitmaps maps each 16-bit Roaring chunk onto pluggable cloud storage tiers. The distinguishing capability
is **serverless chunk-skipping intersection**: `A ∩ B` fetches only the chunks that can possibly contribute,
so intersecting two 2,000,000-id segments touches only the shared chunks, and `count()` on a published
segment does zero payload reads.

Install `@cloudbitmaps/roaring` — `@cloudbitmaps/core` (the codec-agnostic engine plus all ten storage
drivers) arrives transitively. Ten backends ship as optional-peer subpaths: S3, GCS, Azure Blob, DynamoDB,
Postgres, Redis, MongoDB, Cassandra, MySQL, and local filesystem.

## Measured, not modelled

Benchmarked against real S3 + DynamoDB in us-east-1 — not an emulator — with DynamoDB capacity taken from
AWS's own ConsumedCapacity: $0.75 per million incremental writes, $0.14 per million count()s, $5.88 per
million segment publishes, against an always-on Redis-HA line of $346/month standing.

## When NOT to use it

If you need a sub-millisecond p99 on a working set that fits a bounded hot cache, use Redis: a check that
misses the hot cache costs a network round trip, where an in-process RAM store costs a memory read. CloudBitmaps is for sets
that are large, mostly read, and shouldn't cost $346/month to keep warm. In-region latency is not yet
calibrated and no in-region figure is published.

## Status

v0.7.0, Apache-2.0, published tokenlessly with SLSA build provenance. Pre-1.0: breaking changes are possible
in a minor bump until the .crbm format freezes at 1.0.
